context:
Goal: degen's native suite runs once per batch, on the Mac, and you can trust that it ran (degen rule tests-once-per-batch).
Problem (rule): degen's check native_ci_check has never caught a real mistake; its one near-hit (a shell-test job on a Mac runner, 10-30) would have been a false alarm. The real gap is elsewhere: the Mac pass is a line someone types in the PR body, and native-check builds the UI tests but never runs them (the Makefile runs build-for-testing).
Based on (read): degen debt batch-native-tests-manual says its fix is "the Mac run writes its own record line, so no person types it".
Based on (read): the shared iOS standard (claude-settings skill ios-apps) wants kit tests and a compile on a hosted Mac per PR, which degen's check forbids. No ruling for that row was found.
Based on (ruling): you picked 200 a at 2026-11-04 00:21 CST: native-check runs the UI tests (lane native-check-ui-tests, not merged). b's UI step is that ruling, not a new ask.
Departs from: degen main (a typed pass line; UI tests never run in a batch) — b makes the Mac run post its own pass on the commit and narrows the check; c moves kit tests and a compile to a hosted Mac on each PR and deletes the check.

You narrowed this to b or c (17:44 CST); a and d are dropped.

lastAnswer.note: Routed 07:47 CST Nov 5 to the coordinator for a degen lane.

options.gain: GitHub ties the proof to the commit; the debt retires; the suite really runs once per batch with no CI minutes.
options.how: The Mac run posts a native-check status on the exact commit only when it passes; native-record reads that status, not the PR body. The UI tests run through the shared sim-test, as 200 a ruled. Narrow the check to Swift and Xcode commands only; keep its other two clauses, which stop the full suite running twice.
options.label: Machine-written record
options.lose: One build lane; it still trusts the Mac session; UI tests make the Mac run longer and need a simulator lease.

options.gain: Matches home and the shared probe.
options.how: A hosted Mac runs kit tests and a compile on each PR; UI tests stay on the Mac; delete the check.
options.label: Adopt the shared ios-apps standard
options.lose: Paid CI minutes (35 native merges in 14 days; minutes per run unmeasured); kit tests run twice unless native-check drops them.

ref: Opus agent report via the coordinator, 2026-11-04 08:10 CST; degen debt batch-native-tests-manual; degen rule tests-once-per-batch
reply: Your pick b is with the coordinator for a degen lane. The Mac run posts its own pass status on the exact commit, the UI tests run through sim-test, and the check narrows to Swift and Xcode commands. This item closes when that lane merges.
title: degen: how should the Mac prove its native (Swift) suite ran once per batch?
why: GitHub ties the pass to the exact commit, the open debt retires, and the UI tests finally run, with no paid CI minutes.
